rationale:
bugs_open/283 round 7 — round 6's REVISE answered objection by objection, measurements first. The plan is round 6's with two hardenings both seats asked for (a DB-enforced 486-before-487 precondition; pod-binary symbol verification with present+absent controls in 487's header) and edit 7 re-filed as config_change naming its agent row.

(1) guardian MEDIUM 'which other pipelines dispatch fix_component_template' — MEASURED: exactly ONE live workflow references the action (SELECT type FROM agent_definitions WHERE active AND config LIKE '%"fix_component_template"%' → component-template-fixer only; the sub_workflow census query returns zero rows). tool-improver writes through update_component_html, a different action. The new case arms are literal strings no existing caller sends.

(2) guardian HIGH + render_guardian MEDIUM + editquality MEDIUM (owned-page delivery unverified; canary not an edit) — three answers. (a) CORRECTION: 487's success does NOT rest on the owned path. All 14 serving-broken placements sit on GENERIC pages (census 2026-08-19, rebuild_policy per placement); the owned placements among the 32 dirty rows serve PRE-conversion bytes, so repairing their templates leaves them exactly in §13.6's decided posture (delivery on the owning pipeline's next render, or a targeted section_edit) — nothing regresses if the owned path were never used. (b) MEASURED: apply_section_edit already delivers on owned pages in production — 19 section_edit items COMPLETE on rebuild_policy='owned' pages (tool-improver's own delivery step, the sanctioned owned-page path per its step description). The landmine cited ('both sanctioned actions refuse on owned') describes save_page_sections' GENERIC save — §13.6's 15 cancelled items — not the targeted section-editor path. (c) CODE-VERIFIED: the [UNVERIFIED] tag on empty field_updates was too broad — applyContentEdit (section_editor_actions.go:793-850) accepts an empty map (fieldUpdates != nil → merge mode, 0 fields) and then unconditionally re-renders from component html_template; an empty edit is structurally NOT a no-op. What remains runtime-pending is only end-to-end deploy on the LMC estate, which is exactly why the canary is sequenced FIRST — it is an execution artefact (the first item through the 486 branch), not a repo edit, and its evidence lands in the lane NOTES before the LMC batch.

(3) render_guardian HIGH 'does the generic rerender carry a reason?' — MEASURED at the live config and at runtime: create_rerender's INSERT (migs 460/461/462, read back live) builds spec with 'reason','template_changed'; check_rerender_mode routes template_changed to the sections path; proven by the canary (stored render flipped, 34 instance-scoped ids served) and the 53 completed sections-path rerenders of §13.7. The repair arm returns fixed:true through the SAME chain (check_needs_rerender → create_rerender), so all 27 mechanical repairs auto-file page-scoped reason-carrying rerenders. This machinery is the round-4/5 approved work; the repair rides it unchanged.

(4) editquality MEDIUM 'one item per row cannot cover cross-site placements' — the ITEM's site_id is bookkeeping; the repair writes the SHARED template once, and delivery fans out via create_rerender's join over page_components with NO site filter (WHERE pc.component_id = $1 … every page, every site). Concrete: row 795c34e6 (2 sites) → one item, one template write, two page-scoped rerenders. The dedup NOT EXISTS keys on item_key, not site.

(5) reuse_agent MEDIUM 'JudgedConversionIssues re-implements the gate' — FALSE at the code: check 1 IS a call to GateConvertedTemplate (component_instance_judged.go), check 4 IS a call to UnprefixedBindings, and the rename/detect pair share concatSitePatterns by construction so they cannot disagree. The only judged-specific checks are the ones the mechanical gate cannot ask (markup parity and id-set parity are baseline-vs-candidate questions; the mechanical gate has no candidate). BindingIDSets exists because the REPAIR path must recover ids from an ALREADY-CONVERTED template (prefixed declarations), which passes 1-4's in-function seen-map structurally cannot; pass 5 extends the same ConvertTemplateToInstanceScope flow, same declared-id predicate.

(6) bug_historian MEDIUM (locks) — MEASURED: LMC (the judged estate's main target) has 0 locked page_components; round 5's 53-page side-effect sweep measured 0 locked-section duplication on the identical delivery path; section-list lock honouring is governed estate-wide by RFC_033's reader-coverage lockstep (LOCK-008). The canary re-checks this on its own page before the batch. bug_historian MEDIUM (does the repair rerender?) — answered in (3).

(7) llm_reliability MEDIUM (root ai_service shadowing) — MEASURED: the fixer's default_config has NO root ai_service and none under workflow (both false); the step-level 32000 is authoritative. The thinking-budget note is accepted: a thinking-exhausted refusal is the chosen failure direction; refusal rate is a canary observable.

(8) debug_historian MEDIUM (no backup before batch) — MEASURED FALSE: component_versions holds exactly 69 pre-images with change_source='scope_component_instance' (one per converted row — the batch's backups), and writeScopedTemplate takes a NEW pre-image per repair under change_source='repair_instance_scope_bindings' before every write. The risk-3 'snapshot rollback' names those existing rows. debug_historian MEDIUM (digest vs binary) — 487's header now carries the /proc/1/exe symbol grep with a present AND an absent control.

(9) guardian MEDIUM + architecture LOW (ordering not enforced) — 487 now opens with a DO block that RAISES unless the fixer's workflow carries 486's steps; a manual apply-order mistake fails inside the transaction.

(10) guardian LOW (config_change) — edit 7 re-filed as config_change against agent_definitions.type='component-template-fixer' (one active row, snapshot_agent pre-image in the migration).

(11) tooling_provenance MEDIUM — the travelling record exists and closed this loop: the lane's standing five (PLAN_2026-08-18_judged_pipeline.md + 08-19 addendum, NOTES session 6, README, RUNBOOK) and case-file §14 were updated and committed WITH the code (ffef54338); the fixer's own compose_note→append_note steps write a doc_notes row per item; round 7's continuation pointer is bugs_open/283_CONTINUE_HERE_2026-08-19.md. bug_historian's architecture note (one shared fan-out gate for both rewrite paths) is recorded in CLC-022's relations as the open question for a human, alongside architecture's matching 'name the section_edit chain as shared infrastructure next time'.

plan.risks: (1) Markup-parity check may false-refuse on cosmetic LLM reformatting — chosen failure direction is refuse-to-human, never write; relax only on evidence (stated in the design). (2) apply_section_edit end-to-end deploy on an LMC owned page is runtime-pending (code-verified not a no-op: section_editor_actions.go:793-850; 19 production completions on owned pages elsewhere) on that estate — the canary is designed to prove it before the batch (PLAN §5). (3) The 4 serving automation-savings placements stay live-broken until the judged pipeline runs — if it slips, the contained alternative is a snapshot rollback of 3 rows + rerender (owner call, named in bugs_open/324). (4) Migration/seed are _HOLD: applying before the roll dispatches unknown fix_types; the files' headers carry the digest-verify precondition.
